instructions.primary_message: This recipe makes about 10 cups of ragù or 8 (1-1 1/4 cup) servings.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
3 stick celery
½ small pkg fresh basil

instructions.primary_message: Peel, trim, and small dice carrots; trim and small dice celery. Place both in a medium bowl and set aside.
Preheat a large pot over medium-high heat.
While the pot heats up, pat beef dry with paper towels, then season with salt and pepper.
instructions.secondary_message:
1.36 kg beef for stew
1 tsp salt
½ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Once the pot is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Working in batches, add beef and cook, turning occasionally, until golden brown, 4-5 minutes (the beef will not be cooked through). Transfer to a plate. (Reserve pot with drippings for later use.)
Meanwhile, peel, halve, and small dice onions. Peel and mince garlic. Add both to the bowl with the other veggies.
When the beef is done, return pot (with drippings) to medium-high heat. Add veggies and salt; cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, 5-6 minutes.

Return browned beef (and any accumulated juices) to the pot along with tomatoes, broth, bay leaves, and spices. Stir to combine the ragù and bring to a boil. Once boiling, reduce heat to low and simmer, stirring occasionally, until the beef is very tender and ragù is thickened, 2-2 ½ hours.
instructions.secondary_message:
2 (794 g) can canned whole tomatoes
2 cups beef broth
2 tsp Italian seasoning
1 tsp oregano, dried
½ tsp salt
½ tsp black pepper
½ tsp crushed red pepper

instructions.primary_message: When the ragù is almost done, pick basil leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons.

When the ragù is done, remove from heat and discard bay leaves. Using a slotted spoon, transfer beef to a medium bowl. Using two forks, shred beef into smaller pieces. Return beef to the pot, along with basil and vinegar, then stir to combine. Set aside to cool to room temperature, stirring occasionally, about 30 minutes.
Once the ragù has cooled to room temperature, divide between containers.

STORING: Cover each container with an air-tight lid (or wrap tightly with plastic wrap). Place in the freezer for up to 3 months. 



HEATING: For best results, thaw ragù in the fridge overnight. Warm in a saucepan set over medium-high heat, stirring occasionally, until heated through, 8-10 minutes.
CHEF'S NOTE: Serve ragù over warm pasta, topped with freshly grated Parmesan and additional fresh basil, if desired!
